basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 7.' and it opens '(Vers. 7.) Et revertentes venerunt ad fontem judicii, haec est Cades. Per anticipationem'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 7.) Et revertentes venerunt ad fontem judicii, haec est Cades. Per anticipationem dicitur, quod postea sic vocatum est. Significat autem locum apud Petram, qui fons judicii nominatur: quia ibi Deus populum judicavit. Et percusserunt omnem regionem Amalecitarum et Amorrhaeorum sedentem in Asasonthamar. Hoc oppidum est, quod nunc vocatur Engaddi, balsami et palmarum fertile. Porro Asasonthamar, in lingua nostra resonat, urbs Palmarum. Thamar quippe palma dicitur. Sciendum autem pro eo, quod post paululum sequitur: Et direxerunt contra eos aciem ad bellum in valle Salinarum, in Hebraeo haberi, in valle SEDDIM (שדים): quod Aquila interpretatur τῶν περιπεδίνων, Theodotio, τῶν ἀλσῶν, amoena nemora significantes.
